attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, in his voice.

semantics.note: Keeps 'invariably', 'for any given problem' and 'rarely trustworthy'. It is a firm, present-tense description of LLMs, so it is an observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: answers consistently sound right for the task, but dependable answers are uncommon. It does not demand perfection and sets no cutoff for 'rarely'. That is fair, but the result still turns on how 'rarely' is read.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed Nature study from Sept 2024. It finds plausible-sounding wrong answers and unreliability, but it covers earlier model families and does not measure how often dependable answers occur across ordinary tasks at the Jan 2025 snapshot.
Anthropic's own disclosure of an internal agentic coding eval (64% solved). It is selected and not independent, it covers one task type, and it does not measure general trustworthiness.

reviews.rationale: No item in the packet measures both how appropriate the language is and how dependable the answers are across a representative mix of tasks at the target snapshot. e1 supports a reliability concern but not that dependable answers were rare. e2 is a narrow company figure. Neither settles whether answers were rarely trustworthy or whether appropriate language was invariable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'every' and the limit to declarations 'I have seen'. 'Redefining downwards' is an evaluative judgement.

contract.note: The contract correctly notes that the set of declarations he saw is private and that 'downwards' depends on which baseline definition is chosen. Treating the claim as uncheckable is fair to his words.

evidence.note: Dec 2024 report of an OpenAI employee declaring AGI on a 'most humans at most tasks' standard. It is one example consistent with the pattern and cannot settle a universal claim about what Marcus saw.
The 2023 Noema essay declaring AGI is here, framed as generality. Whether that counts as 'downwards' is a judgement call. It is labelled a secondary summary, but it is the original essay.

reviews.rationale: The claim is limited to declarations Marcus personally saw, and no public list of them exists. It also depends on an evaluative baseline for 'redefining downwards'. The individual declarations in the packet are context only and cannot test a universal claim about his private reading, so it cannot be scored.
